A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the evolution in viral load is predictive for the natural history of a single‐type HPV infection, with persistent high‐grade cervical disease developing from infections with an almost constant high viral load.
the natural history of high‐risk HPV infections can be predicted by measuring type‐specific HPV load over time, which is a promising tool to improve HPV‐based cervical screening.

the slope in viral load changes can be used to distinguish HPV infections leading to cancer from transient infections.

the natural history of persistent high‐risk human HPV infection is characterized by a linear increase in HPV viral load over time, while transient high‐risk HPV infections are associated with an increasing or decreasing viral load profile.
